key_insight: A three-modal fusion model combining ultrasound images, clinical attributes, and report text improved fine-grained separation of fibroadenoma and phyllodes tumors.
clinical_relevance: This could support more accurate preoperative risk stratification for fibroepithelial breast lesions that look similar on ultrasound.
method: Built the FAPT-M dataset with 910 pathology-confirmed patients and reviewed ultrasound, clinical, and text data.
Used DenseNet for image encoding, CLIP-inspired text encoding, and lightweight clinical feature encoding.
Added clinical-conditioned modulation, cross-modal Transformer fusion, and dual-path representation learning.
evidence_signal: In patient-level five-fold cross-validation, the model reached 77.64% accuracy, 73.38% F1-score, and 89.74% AUC, outperforming multiple baseline CNN, Transformer, and vision-language methods.
watch_item: Results come from a single curated dataset, so external validation is needed before broader clinical use.
paper_title: Multimodal Fusion for Fine-Grained Classification of Breast Fibroadenoma and Phyllodes Tumors
